name: Malawisuchus
sum: Malawisuchus is a small notosuchian crocodyliform from the Early Cretaceous Dinosaur Beds of Malawi, with mammal-like teeth.
holotype: Not stated in the sources consulted for this draft; first discovered in 1989 and described by Gomani in 1997.
material: Several specimens, including articulated ones, from the Dinosaur Beds of northern Malawi.
biology: Its rear teeth had several cusps; hind-limb joints suggest an upright posture and running ability, muscle attachments on the upper arm suggest digging, and articulated specimens appear to have been preserved in burrows.
author: Gomani 1997

sources.text: Gomani, Elizabeth M. 1997. A crocodyliform from the Early Cretaceous Dinosaur Beds, northern Malawi. Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology 17(2): 280–294. doi:10.1080/02724634.1997.10010975
